attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: An unhedged claim about an ongoing trend. The normalised wording matches the sentence. No condition or horizon is stated.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. It treats this as a general trend, takes size to mean parameters, and reads cost as task-level inference cost, which follows the context about token burn. The September 2024 window is inferred but reasonable. Which meanings of size and cost are used affects the result.

evidence.note: A company disclosure about one model family. It says Qwen3 gets similar performance with fewer active parameters. It does not show the market-wide trend in total size or in task costs.

Independent data on per-token prices at a fixed capability level, mostly before the window (ends October 2024). Per-token prices leave out reasoning-token volume, so this does not settle task-level cost.

reviews.rationale: Neither item gives a matched series of model sizes and task-level inference costs across 2024-25 releases. One is a single company's disclosure and the other measures per-token prices from an earlier period. Neither establishes or refutes the claimed trend toward bigger, more expensive models.

attribution.note: Zitron's own rebuttal of a booster argument, in his voice.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the carve-out for construction and the vague word 'much'. It is an unhedged observation.

contract.note: Reading the claim as the growth contribution from operations, net of construction, fits his words. Using Q2 2025 is inferred but reasonable. 'Much' has no threshold, and whether 'building costs' includes equipment is unclear.

evidence.note: St. Louis Fed figures on investment contributions for Q2 2025, published before the evaluation date. They measure construction and investment, not operations, so they fall inside his carve-out.
Finds that construction drives most of the benefit, which points in his direction. But it covers all Virginia data centers in an earlier period, not US AI facilities in the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: Neither item isolates the contribution of US AI data-center operations to growth in Q2 2025. e5 measures only investment, and e6 differs in geography, scope and period. With no threshold for 'much', the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own causal explanation, in his voice.

semantics.note: The sentence answers 'Why Did This Happen?' about rising token burn and cost. The normalised wording keeps both the diminishing-returns cause and the 'only way' exclusivity.

contract.note: 'The only way' is the speaker's own exclusive wording, so testing it against an alternative route to improvement is fair. Technical reports are acceptable sources under this contract.

evidence.note: Qwen3 technical report, May 2025, before the post. Base models improve through data, architecture and training before any reasoning post-training. That shows another route. These are self-reported benchmarks.
DeepSeek-R1, January 2025. Longer chain-of-thought improves reasoning tasks. This supports only the narrow point that reasoning helps, not that it was the only route.

reviews.rationale: The contract's first contradiction condition is met. e1 is a pre-publication technical comparison showing capability gains from pretraining changes, independent of burning more inference tokens. That undercuts 'the only way'. The packet does not measure how much of any cost increase came from reasoning, but the explicit exclusivity fails.

semantics.note: 'Lies of inference', followed by 'Ironic, I know', is a pun. The surrounding section is about user and customer metrics and inferring usefulness from popularity, not about capabilities. The normalised wording narrows it to capability implications that the speaker did not state.

contract.note: The contract supplies a capability-misrepresentation reading and a period starting in 2022, neither of which the speaker gave. The context points to inferences drawn from user counts. The words are too vague to set a fair test.

evidence.note: The ChatGPT launch post discloses that answers can be unreliable. It shows qualified marketing but does not test the claim.
Promotional language for ChatGPT agent, July 2025, alongside limitations. It does not settle whether the marketing misled.
Anthropic's 2023 launch post, marketing capabilities with qualified language. It is not a matched comparison with actual capability.

reviews.rationale: The statement is a rhetorical pun ('lies of inference') with no specific misrepresentation, population or measure. The context suggests it refers to inferences from user metrics, not capability claims. Too vague to score fairly; the packet would not settle it under any reading.
